title: Prefix sums, 2D prefix sums & difference arrays
relevance: High — static range sums, subarray-sum counting, and range updates are among the most common OA / interview array patterns; CF Div2 B–C reuse the same templates constantly.
company_notes: Immutable many range-sum queries (LC 303 / CSES Static Range Sum); range increments then report the array (LC 1109 / Car Pooling-style difference); count subarrays with sum K or sum divisible by K (LC 560 / CSES Subarray Sums II & Divisibility, Amazon/Google-style); any submatrix/block sum (LC 304 / CSES Forest Queries).

phases.goal: Establish when the candidate reaches for 1D/2D prefix sums, difference arrays, or prefix+hash instead of naive loops or a tree.

must_hit.point: Immutable array with many range-sum queries → precompute 1D prefix sums (NumArray / static range sum).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names LC 303 / CSES Static Range Sum or says build prefixes so each query is a two-prefix difference.

must_hit.point: Many range updates then one (or few) reads of the final array → difference array, not per-update loops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions mark +v/−v on endpoints (bookings, seats, timeline capacity) then one prefix rebuild.

must_hit.point: Count subarrays with sum K or sum divisible by m → prefix values hashed (or prefix mod m), not O(n²) enumeration.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Points to LC 560 / CSES Subarray Sums II or Divisibility and map of prefixes / remainders.

must_hit.point: Sum of any submatrix/block on a static grid → 2D prefix with rectangle inclusion–exclusion.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names LC 304 / Forest Queries or says integral image / 2D prefix for rectangle queries.

probes: You get an immutable array and many sum(l..r) queries—what do you precompute, and when would you instead use a difference array?
How do you recognize a 'count subarrays with property X on sums' problem versus a plain range-sum API?

hints.1: Think about whether the array is static with range reads, or you batch range writes first.
hints.2: Static many queries → prefix; many range updates then read → diff; subarray count by sum/mod → prefix map.
hints.3: Say: sum(l..r)=pref[r]−pref[l−1]; updates via diff[l]+=v, diff[r+1]−=v; subarray K via map of prefixes.

phases.goal: Get the candidate to state the 1D, difference, 2D, and prefix-hash templates before coding details.

must_hit.point: Contiguous range sum is a constant-time difference of two prefixes: sum(l..r)=pref[r]−pref[l−1].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes that identity and mentions consistent 0- or 1-indexing with an empty-prefix sentinel.

must_hit.point: Difference array: mark +v at l and −v at r+1; one prefix of diff applies many range updates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes endpoint marks then rebuild; may cite Water Heater / Corporate Flight Bookings.

must_hit.point: 2D: build with inclusion–exclusion on cells; query a rectangle with +/−/+ inclusion–exclusion on four corners.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States P[i][j]=a[i][j]+P[i−1][j]+P[i][j−1]−P[i−1][j−1] and the matching rectangle query signs.

must_hit.point: Same-remainder prefixes (pref % m, negatives normalized) mean a divisible subarray; subarray sum K uses frequencies of prior prefixes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Links same mod ⇒ divisible block and counting via map lookups of pref−K.

probes: State the 1D range-sum identity and the difference-array update rule.
How do you extend the idea to rectangle sums and to counting subarrays with sum K?

hints.1: Range sum is two prefixes; range add is two endpoint marks.
hints.2: Spell sum(l..r)=pref[r]−pref[l−1] and diff[l]+=v, diff[r+1]−=v, then prefix(diff).
hints.3: Add 2D P build/query inclusion–exclusion and 'hash prefixes / pref%m' for counting variants.

phases.goal: Check they can write the concrete builds, query order for hash maps, and 2D formulas without off-by-one handwaving.

must_hit.point: Build 1D with pref[0]=0 and pref[i]=pref[i−1]+a[i]; answer ranges as pref[r]−pref[l−1] with consistent indexing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows the sentinel zero prefix and the subtraction formula in code-shaped steps.

must_hit.point: Difference: diff[l]+=v, diff[r+1]−=v; final array is the prefix of diff (use long long on CF).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions r+1 mark, clamp/bounds care, and long long for contest overflow.

must_hit.point: Subarray sum = K: frequency map of prefixes; init {0:1}; query pref−K before inserting the current pref.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly says look up pref−K first, then insert; starts with empty-prefix count 1.

must_hit.point: 2D build P[i][j]=a[i][j]+P[i−1][j]+P[i][j−1]−P[i−1][j−1]; rectangle query uses the matching inclusion–exclusion.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the four-term build and four-corner query pattern.

probes: Walk through building pref with pref[0]=0 and answering one sum(l..r).
For subarray sum K, in what order do you query and update the prefix frequency map?

hints.1: Start from the empty prefix and the two-line update for a range add.
hints.2: Write pref[0]=0; for K, map starts {0:1} and checks pref−K before insert.
hints.3: Also state diff[l]+=v / diff[r+1]−=v and the full 2D P recurrence.

phases.goal: Confirm they know prefix/diff give constant-time range answers after a linear-style precompute, and when that stops being enough.

must_hit.point: After prefix precompute, any contiguous range sum is O(1) (constant-time difference of two prefixes).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says each query is pref[r]−pref[l−1] in O(1), matching Range Sum Query Immutable / CSES static sums.

must_hit.point: Difference array applies many range updates via endpoint marks then one prefix rebuild; interleaved updates+queries need Fenwick/segment tree instead.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts batch updates→diff vs online interleaved updates→tree (next topic).

probes: After you build the prefix array, what is the per-query cost for sum(l..r)?
When do you abandon difference/prefix for a Fenwick or segment tree?

hints.1: Focus on query cost once prefixes exist, and on update/query interleaving.
hints.2: O(1) per static range sum; many updates then one read stays with diff+one prefix.
hints.3: Static many queries → prefix O(1); batch range adds → diff; interleaved updates → Fenwick/segment tree.

phases.goal: Surface off-by-one, overflow, mod normalization, and map-update order mistakes that break these templates.

must_hit.point: Off-by-one discipline: inclusive bounds, r+1 clamp, empty-prefix sentinel, and overflow (long long on CF).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out r+1 marking, sentinel pref[0]=0, and 64-bit sums on Codeforces.

must_hit.point: For subarray sum K, inserting pref before querying pref−K double-counts or misses; for divisibility, normalize negative pref%m.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States query-before-insert and positive remainder normalization for mods.

must_hit.point: Prefix/suffix aggregates are not only sums—products, GCD, XOR, or pattern counts need the same left/right combine idea without assuming + only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Product of Array Except Self, prefix/suffix GCD, or counting "AC" / peaks via specialized prefixes.

probes: What off-by-one and overflow bugs do you watch for on difference arrays in contests?
What goes wrong if you update the prefix frequency map before looking up pref−K?

hints.1: Think endpoints of inclusive ranges and empty prefix.
hints.2: r+1 must be in range or clamped; always long long on CF; map lookup before insert.
hints.3: List: inclusive bounds, r+1 clamp, pref[0]=0, overflow, query pref−K before insert, normalize negative mods.

tradeoffs.topic: Prefix sums vs difference arrays vs Fenwick/segment tree
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Many range queries on static data → prefix sums; many range updates then one read → difference array; interleaved updates and queries → Fenwick or segment tree (next topic).

gotchas.trap: Off-by-one on inclusive ranges when marking difference updates or subtracting prefixes.
gotchas.correction: Keep indexing consistent; use empty-prefix sentinel pref[0]=0; for updates mark +v at l and −v at r+1 with clamp.

gotchas.trap: Overflow on CF when summing or applying many range adds.
gotchas.correction: Use long long for difference arrays and prefix sums under contest constraints.

gotchas.trap: Updating the prefix frequency map before querying pref−K when counting subarrays with sum K.
gotchas.correction: Init map with {0:1}; query count of pref−K first, then insert the current pref.

gotchas.trap: Using raw negative values for pref % m in divisibility problems.
gotchas.correction: Hash normalized pref % m so same remainder correctly means a divisible block.
